html:
The Yoncalla were the southernmost Kalapuya people, living in the hills and valleys of the upper Umpqua basin in western Oregon, near today's town of Yoncalla. They spoke Southern Kalapuya, the most distinct of the Kalapuyan languages.

They hunted deer and elk, burned the valley grasslands to keep them open, and gathered camas and acorns. Settlers came along the Applegate Trail, a southern branch of the Oregon Trail, from 1846. In the 1850s the Yoncalla signed treaties and were moved to the Grand Ronde Reservation; their descendants belong to the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde. Their neighbours to the south were the Cow Creek Umpqua.
